questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India sets out the different Fundamental Duties for Indian citizens?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Article 51A** sets out the different **Fundamental Duties** for Indian citizens.
 
• The moral duty of all people to support the growth of **patriotism and the preservation** of India's unity is referred to as the Fundamental Duties.

 
• The Indian Constitution's **Part IVA** governs Fundamental Duties.
 
• There are currently **eleven** fundamental duties.
 
• The Constitution was amended by the **42nd and 86th Constitutional Amendment Acts**, adding basic duties.
 
• The Constitution requires citizens to carry out their duties in an **ethical manner.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moral and civic duties **are the two categories into which fundamental duties fall.

 
 
• Moral duty includes upholding the lofty goals of the **freedom movement.**
 
• **Respecting** the Constitution, the flag, and the national anthem is a civic duty.
 
 
 
• Unlike several other Fundamental Rights, the Fundamental Duties are **exclusive to Indian nationals **and do not apply to foreigners.
 
• Similar to the Directive Principles of State Policy, they are likewise **nonjusticiable.**
 
• There is** no legal repercussion** for their transgression.

questions.question: Articles 52 to 78 in Part V of the Indian Constitution deal with ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Executive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Articles 52 to 78 in Part V of the Indian Constitution deal with the Union Executive.
 
• The Union Executive consists of the President, the Vice-President, the Prime Minister, the Council of Ministers, and the Attorney General of India.
 
• The President of India is the head of the Union Executive and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• Articles 52 to 62 deal with the President, Articles 63 to 71 deal with the Vice-President, Articles 74 and 75 deal with the Council of Ministers, and Articles 76 and 78 deal with the Attorney General of India and the duties of the Prime Minister.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Finance Commission of India**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body for the purpose of allocation of certain revenue resources between the Union and the State Governments.
 
• It was established under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Finance Commission is appointed every five years and consists of a chairman and four other members.
 
 
 
• **Amendment of the Constitution**
 
 
• The procedure for the amendment of the Constitution is laid down in Article 368 in Part XX of the Constitution.
 
• It provides for a flexible procedure for the amendment to address the changing needs and circumstances of the country.
 
• An amendment can be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill in either House of Parliament and must be passed by a special majority.
 
 
 
• **National Emergency**
 
 
• National emergency provisions are contained in Article 352 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• A National Emergency can be declared on the grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• During a National Emergency, the federal structure of the country changes to a unitary one, and the central government becomes more powerful.

• The Directive Principles of State Policy are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• DPSP serve as guidelines for the central and state governments of India, which are intended to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• Though not enforceable by any court, these principles are considered fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Examples of DPSP include securing a living wage, ensuring equal pay for equal work, promoting the health and strength of workers, and fostering respect for international law and treaty obligations.

• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 provided a constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions and brought them under the purview of the justiciable part of the Constitution.
 
• This amendment aimed at creating a uniform structure of Panchayati Raj throughout India and ensuring more powers and responsibilities to these bodies.

questions.question: Which of the following Rights is mentioned in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty
Right against Exploitation: Prohibition of trafficking in human beings and forced labour
Right to Equality: Equality before law

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 21 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the **Right to Protection of life and personal liberty** to all citizens and non-citizens.
 
• It states, "No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law."
 
• This article ensures that the State cannot take away a person's life or liberty arbitrarily without following due process of law.
 
• It encompasses a wide range of rights, including the right to live with human dignity, right to privacy, and right to a healthy environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Privacy**

 
 
• In the landmark judgment of *Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) vs Union of India* (2017), the Supreme Court of India declared the right to privacy as a fundamental right under Article 21.
 
• This judgment has significant implications for data protection and individual autonomy in India.
 
 
 
• **Right to a Healthy Environment**
 
 
• Article 21 has been interpreted by the judiciary to include the right to a pollution-free environment, which is essential for living a quality life.
 
• Environmental protection and sustainability have been integrated into the right to life and personal liberty.
 
 
 
• **Right to Legal Aid**
 
 
• The right to free legal aid is considered an integral part of Article 21 to ensure that justice is accessible to all, irrespective of economic status.
 
• The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, implements this right by providing free legal services to the weaker sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Right to Live with Human Dignity**
 
 
• The Supreme Court has expanded Article 21 to include the right to live with dignity, which encompasses adequate nutrition, clothing, shelter, and proper healthcare.
 
• This broader interpretation aims at ensuring a decent standard of living for every individual.
